summary_paragraph: A male patient with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and chronic systolic heart failure was admitted due to recurrent hypoglycemia and syncope, occurring just two days after a prior discharge for the same issue. He was found unconscious at home with a blood sugar of 28 despite correct insulin administration. During the hospital stay, his insulin regimen was simplified by switching from NPH insulin to Lantus, starting at 5 units and titrating up to 6 units daily, along with 1 unit of Humalog with each meal to reduce hypoglycemia risk. His lanthanum dose was increased to 1,500 mg with meals due to elevated phosphorus and PTH levels, and his multivitamin was discontinued. He remained stable, completed a hemodialysis session, and was discharged home with close follow-up, new insulin instructions, and additional diabetes education support.
problems: Poor glycemic control in type 1 diabetes
